title: One detailed session and PR status on every session row
prompt:
Session rows (sidebar, overview, dashboard, phone) only show lifecycle status. Show one detailed status per row that combines what the agent needs and the state of the branch's pull request, decided in one place that the desktop, the phone and the Rust CLI all share.

Shared decision (packages/portable):
- Add `@terminalx/portable/sessionStatus` (packages/portable/src/sessionStatus.ts, exported from the package). Inputs: `SessionStatusInput = { tabs: { status: "idle"|"in_progress"|"completed"|"waiting"; activity?: "needs_permission"|"needs_answer"|"review_plan"|"setting_up"|"setup_failed"|"stopping"|"background"|null }[]; branch?: string|null; branchStatus?: { branch: string; checked: boolean; headMatches?: boolean|null; pr?: { number; state; draft; mergeable; mergeStateStatus; checks: string|null; inMergeQueue } | null } | null }`.
- Export `sessionStatus(input)` returning exactly `{ id, label, icon, color, tooltip }` (all non-empty, input not mutated), `combinedSessionStatus(inputs)` for a collapsed row of several sessions (the highest-precedence status among them, independent of order), and `SESSION_STATUSES` (every status description, in precedence order).
- Keep the rules as data in packages/portable/src/sessionStatusRules.json so Rust can read the same table.
- branchStatus only counts when `checked` is true and its `branch` equals the session's `branch`; otherwise it is ignored.
- Precedence, first match wins (id: label):
  needs_permission: Needs permission (any tab activity needs_permission); needs_answer: Needs answer; review_plan: Review plan; setup_failed: Setup failed; needs_attention: Needs attention (a tab waiting with no activity); stopping: Stopping; setting_up: Setting up; working: Working (a tab in_progress); background: Waiting on background task;
  then the PR: merged: Merged (state MERGED and headMatches true); merge_conflict: Merge conflict (OPEN, mergeable CONFLICTING); checks_failing: Checks failing (OPEN, checks FAILURE or ERROR, even on a draft); in_merge_queue: In merge queue (OPEN, inMergeQueue); draft: Draft (OPEN, draft); checks_running: Checks running (OPEN, checks PENDING or EXPECTED); ready_to_merge: Ready to merge (OPEN, MERGEABLE, mergeStateStatus CLEAN, checks SUCCESS or absent, and headMatches true; unknown mergeability, unpushed or unknown local head is never ready); open_pr: Open PR (any other OPEN); local_only: Local only (checked with no PR, a CLOSED PR, or a MERGED PR whose head no longer matches);
  then completed: Completed (a tab completed); idle: Idle otherwise (also when PR data is missing, unchecked, or for another branch, and for a MERGED PR whose head match is unknown).
- Agent attention always wins over any PR state.

Desktop:
- `api.sessionRowStatuses(ids: string[])` in src/lib/api.ts invokes `session_row_statuses` with `{ ids }` and returns `Record<id, SessionStatusInput>`; implement that command in src-tauri from the sessions' tabs and the cached branch/PR observation.
- src/lib/sessionRowStatus.ts exports `useSessionRowStatus(sessions)` returning the combined status description. All mounted rows share one poll: one batched call with every visible id (deduplicated), first read right after mount, then every 10 seconds; no polling once no rows are mounted. A row re-renders only when its own status changes. If a read fails (runtime lost), drop the remote results so stale verdicts such as Ready to merge disappear and rows fall back to their local lifecycle.
- src/components/ui/SessionStatus.tsx exports `SessionStatus({ session })`, which shows the label (with icon, colour and tooltip) and is used on the sidebar, overview and dashboard rows. Respect the animations preference from `usePrefs`.
- Draw the same status on the phone's session rows, and let the CLI's session list print it.
notes: Modules touched by the change: packages/portable (shared decision table), src/lib and src/components/ui (desktop rows), mobile/src (phone rows), src-tauri (a batched row-status command and the CLI reading the same table). Check: vitest, 2.0 s failing at the start, 1.3 s passing measured by check-task on 2026-11-12 (a fresh pnpm install adds 8 to 17 s; a cached one about 1 s). Start is the merge's first parent; solution is the merge commit.
